headline: President Obama waived certain Trade Act of 1974 rules for Belarus.
what_it_does: This order uses the President's power to waive certain requirements of the Trade Act of 1974 for Belarus. That law includes rules, often called the Jackson-Vanik rules, that limit trade benefits and some US government financing for certain countries based on their emigration policies. A waiver like this usually lets those benefits or programs go ahead. No summary was provided, so the exact scope of this waiver is not clear from the title alone.

who_it_affects.group: US businesses that trade with or invest in Belarus
who_it_affects.how: They may gain access to US government trade financing or support that the Trade Act would otherwise limit.
Belarus is treated as exempt from certain Trade Act requirements because of the waiver.

when_it_takes_effect: Likely when signed on July 1, 2009, though the title does not state an effective date.
